allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

tech_stack.description: Technology stack for the roadmap. Decision rule: include at minimum `languages` and `frameworks`; add `databases`, `queues`, `caches`, `infra`, and `tools` as needed. Example 1 (Python backend): {"languages": ["python"], "frameworks": ["fastapi"], "databases": ["postgresql"], "caches": ["redis"], "infra": ["docker", "github-actions"]}. Example 2 (TypeScript fullstack): {"languages": ["typescript"], "frameworks": ["nextjs", "express"], "databases": ["postgresql"], "infra": ["vercel", "github-actions"]}. Anti-pattern: leaving `tech_stack` empty or omitting `languages` and `frameworks` — these are always required because they define the primary development environment.

allOf.description: Inherits the structured technology stack definition from core collections.

tech_stack_ref.description: Canonical reference to the project's technology stack in the canonical registry. Kind is structurally pinned to 'tech_stack'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:tech_stack:python", "kind": "tech_stack", "label": "Python"}. Define this entry in project canon (canon/manifest.json) before referencing it here. Anti-pattern: inventing a cn: ID without a corresponding canon entry — canonical-lint will fail if the ID is not registered.

milestones.description: Ordered roadmap milestones with user stories, tasks, and deliverables.

milestone_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this milestone. Convention: ms-{phase-or-domain}-{noun}. Decision rule: choose a name that reflects the delivered capability, not a sequential position — IDs must remain stable once tasks reference them, so renaming breaks dependency tracking. Examples: 'ms-auth-mvp' (auth domain, first release), 'ms-payment-integration' (payment domain), 'ms-reporting-phase1' (phased delivery with explicit phase suffix). Anti-pattern: 'ms-1' or 'ms-milestone-a' (sequential labels with no traceable meaning); 'ms-all-features' (too broad to manage — split into domain-scoped milestones).

name.description: Human-readable name of the milestone, distinguishable from all other milestones in this roadmap. Use Title Case, 3–6 words describing the major deliverable theme. Examples: 'Core Authentication API', 'Payment Integration MVP', 'User Profile Management', 'Performance Hardening Sprint', 'Data Migration Phase 1'. Avoid sequential labels ('Milestone 1', 'Phase A') — they carry no semantic meaning. Avoid verb phrases ('Implement Auth') — use noun phrases describing the delivered capability.

target_date.description: Target completion date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Decision rule: set target_date to the sprint end date when the milestone aligns to a sprint; use the agreed delivery date from the project plan otherwise. Examples: '2025-03-31' (end of Q1 sprint), '2025-06-15' (negotiated delivery date for a partner integration). Each milestone should have a distinct date that reflects its actual planned completion. Anti-pattern: setting all milestones to the same date — identical dates signal copy-paste from a template rather than a real plan, and make it impossible to sequence or track progress.

status.description: Current progress status of the milestone. 'pending': not yet started, waiting to begin. 'in_progress': actively being worked on. 'done': all deliverables completed and verified. 'deferred': postponed to a later milestone or release. Use 'pending' for newly created milestones.

risk_status.description: Risk level for this milestone's delivery confidence. Decision rule — 'low': on track, no known blockers; 'medium': risk identified, mitigation in progress, delivery still achievable; 'high': blocker present, delivery at risk without active intervention; 'critical': milestone at risk of failure, escalate to stakeholders immediately. Escalation examples: use 'medium' when a key dependency has slipped by 1 week and a workaround is in progress; use 'high' when a dependency has slipped by 2+ weeks with no confirmed mitigation; use 'critical' when the milestone cannot be delivered in scope without a timeline change decision. Anti-pattern: defaulting to 'low' to avoid escalation — 'medium' and 'high' trigger the review process that surfaces and resolves blockers before they become critical.

user_story.description: User story this milestone addresses. Should follow 'As a <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>' format to tie the milestone to a user-facing outcome.

source_milestones.description: Upstream Step 09 milestone IDs this roadmap milestone maps to. Look up valid IDs in spec/09_impl_plan.json under milestones[*].milestone_id. Examples: ['ms-auth-backend', 'ms-user-profile'] (if this roadmap milestone corresponds to both of those impl plan milestones). Decision rule: include all Step 09 milestones whose deliverables contribute to this roadmap milestone's user story. Omit if the roadmap milestone has no direct Step 09 counterpart (e.g., a discovery milestone with no impl plan deliverables). Anti-pattern: inventing milestone IDs — only reference IDs that exist in spec/09_impl_plan.json.

items.description: An FR ID in the format 'fr-<slug>' referencing a functional requirement.

fr_refs.description: Functional requirement IDs this milestone delivers. Each should match an fr_id in spec/04_fr_list.json (validated by traceability checks). Should contain at least one entry; list all FRs substantially addressed by the milestone's tasks.

items.description: A capability ID in the format 'cap-<slug>' referencing a capability.

capability_refs.description: Capability IDs from spec/01_capabilities.json that this milestone implements.

task_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this task within the parent milestone. Use the pattern 'task-{verb}-{noun}' to make the ID self-describing. Examples: 'task-implement-auth-endpoint', 'task-add-session-schema', 'task-write-login-unit-tests', 'task-deploy-auth-service', 'task-configure-rate-limiting'. The verb names the work type (implement, add, write, migrate, configure, deploy, integrate). Avoid sequential IDs like 'task-1' or 'task-a' — they convey no meaning and break traceability when tasks are reordered.

description.description: What this task accomplishes, at the granularity of a developer story. Describe the user-facing or system-observable outcome, not implementation steps. Scope: one coherent piece of work completable in 1–3 days. Examples: 'Implement POST /auth/login endpoint with JWT issuance and rate limiting', 'Add users table migration with bcrypt password column and soft-delete support', 'Write unit tests for token refresh logic covering expiry and invalid-signature boundary conditions', 'Configure Stripe webhook handler to transition order status on payment confirmation'. Avoid: single-word descriptions ('Implement'), pure technical micro-steps ('Add index'), or commit-message-level details.

acceptance_criteria.description: Conditions that must be met for this task to be considered complete. Each criterion should be objectively verifiable — write them so a reviewer who wasn't present can confirm completion. Examples: 'All unit tests pass with >80% coverage', 'API endpoint responds within 200ms under load test'. Avoid: 'code reviewed', 'looks good', 'done'.

criterion_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this acceptance criterion within the task. Convention: ac-{task_id_slug}-{n} where task_id_slug is the parent task ID without the 'task-' prefix. Examples: 'ac-implement-jwt-auth-1', 'ac-implement-jwt-auth-2'. Anti-pattern: 'ac-1', 'ac-criterion-a' — sequential labels that cannot be traced to the parent task.

text.description: Full text of the acceptance criterion (minimum 15 characters). Decision rule: each criterion should cover a distinct scenario type — happy path, error case, or boundary condition — so that together they provide full coverage of the task's behavior. Happy path example: 'All unit tests pass and line coverage is >= 80%.' Error case example: 'POST /checkout with an expired payment token returns HTTP 402 with error code PAYMENT_EXPIRED.' Boundary condition example: 'A cart with exactly 100 items processes without timeout under nominal load.' Anti-pattern: criteria that only describe happy paths — error cases and boundary conditions must also be specified to prevent regressions.

fixture_ref.description: Kebab-case ID of the fixture from spec/08_fixtures.json that validates this acceptance criterion. Before omitting, verify that no matching fixture exists in Step 08 — missing fixture_ref values create coverage gaps detectable by specdev matrix. If no fixture exists yet and one should, note it as a gap in milestone risks.

items.description: A single acceptance criterion covering one scenario type (happy path, error case, or boundary condition), with an optional fixture reference for automated validation.

status.description: Task-level status: 'pending' (not started), 'in_progress' (actively being worked), 'done' (completed and verified). Note: tasks cannot be 'deferred' — only milestones support deferral. If a task's parent milestone is deferred, the task remains 'pending'.

status_ref.description: Canonical reference to the task status in the canonical registry. Kind is structurally pinned to 'status'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:status:pending", "kind": "status"}. Must be consistent with the task's 'status' field value.

environment_ref.description: Canonical reference to the target environment for this task. Kind must be 'environment'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:environment:staging", "kind": "environment", "label": "staging"}. Use to indicate which environment this task targets for deployment or testing. Common IDs: 'cn:core:environment:dev', 'cn:core:environment:staging', 'cn:core:environment:prod'.

metric_ref.description: Canonical reference to the metric used to measure task completion. Kind is structurally pinned to 'metric'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:metric:error-rate", "kind": "metric", "label": "Error Rate"}. Use when task completion is gated on a measurable metric (e.g., performance benchmark, coverage threshold). Omit for tasks with qualitative acceptance criteria only.

items.description: A task_id that this task depends on within the same milestone.

depends_on.description: task_ids this task depends on (within same milestone). Should not create cycles (validated by tooling).

items.description: An assumption that must hold for this task to succeed (minimum 10 characters).

assumptions.description: Assumptions that must hold for this task to succeed.

items.description: A condition that definitively marks this task complete (minimum 15 characters).

exit_conditions.description: Conditions that definitively mark this task complete.

fr_refs.description: Functional requirement IDs this task addresses. Each should match an fr_id in spec/04_fr_list.json (validated by traceability checks). Enables pairwise completeness checks: verifies every FR has at least one roadmap task. Add all FRs this task contributes to, even partially. Example: ['fr-user-login', 'fr-session-refresh'].

items.description: An FR ID in the format 'fr-<slug>' referencing a functional requirement.

invariant_refs.description: Invariant IDs from Step 06 that this task enforces or tests. Enables traceability from roadmap tasks back to system invariant guarantees. Add all invariants this task validates, even partially.

items.description: A single task within a milestone, with acceptance criteria and dependencies.

tasks.description: Atomic sub-tasks required to complete the user story.

deliverables.description: Trace references to spec artifacts this milestone will produce or modify as deliverables. Use type 'produces' for new artifacts and type 'modifies' for updated artifacts. Example: [{"type": "produces", "id": "fr-user-login", "note": "New FR created in this milestone"}, {"type": "modifies", "id": "cap-user-authentication", "note": "Capability updated to reflect auth scope changes"}]. Anti-pattern: bare strings — deliverables must be typed traceRef objects.

items.description: A trace reference to an artifact this milestone will produce.

risks.description: Known risks that could delay or block this milestone. Each entry should name the specific threat, its probability, and the planned mitigation. Decision rule: write one entry per distinct risk, not one entry per category. Examples: 'Third-party payment API instability — high probability during peak load; mitigate with circuit breaker and fallback to manual processing order queue.' 'Legal review for PII data policy may miss Sprint 3 deadline — medium probability; mitigate by requesting review in Sprint 2 with a two-week buffer.' Anti-pattern: 'Technical risks' or 'Integration risks' (category labels, not named risks — a reviewer cannot act on a category).

spikes.description: Time-boxed technical investigations required to resolve specific uncertainties before work can proceed. Decision rule: each spike entry must name (1) the question being answered, (2) the time budget, and (3) the expected output. Examples: 'Evaluate Redis Cluster vs Elasticache for session store — 2-day spike, output: architectural decision record with latency benchmarks.' 'Prototype JWT rotation with zero-downtime rollover — 1-day spike, output: working proof of concept committed to feature branch.' Anti-pattern: 'Investigate performance' or 'Research options' (open-ended spikes with no time box or defined output cannot be completed or reviewed).

status_ref.description: Canonical reference to the milestone status in the canonical registry. Kind is structurally pinned to 'status'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:status:pending", "kind": "status"}. Must be consistent with the 'status' field value.

items.description: A single roadmap milestone with user story, tasks, and deliverables.

migration_plan.description: High-level strategy for migrating from existing systems or data. A good migration plan addresses four areas: (1) what is being replaced (legacy system, schema version, or API contract); (2) migration sequence (strangler fig pattern vs. big-bang replacement); (3) rollback plan (how to revert if migration fails); (4) acceptance test for successful migration (how to confirm the migration is complete). Example: 'Migrate auth from session cookies to JWT tokens using strangler fig pattern across 3 milestones — existing session auth remains active until milestone 3; rollback: re-enable session middleware; acceptance: all auth endpoints accept JWT tokens and all legacy session tests pass.' Anti-pattern: 'We will migrate the data' (does not describe sequence, rollback, or acceptance criteria).

dependencies.description: External or internal dependencies required by the roadmap. Uses structured dependency objects (each with type, id, and optional owner/note fields) — not simple string IDs. Contrast with Step 09 impl_plan which uses dependencyList (mixed string/object). Every entry here must be a full object.

dependency_ref.description: Canonical reference to the primary external or cross-team dependency this roadmap depends on. Kind must be 'dependency'. Decision rule: use this field to reference a single canonical dependency entry that gates the entire roadmap; use the milestone-level `risks` and `deliverables` fields for per-milestone dependency notes. Cross-team example: {"id": "cn:project:dependency:auth-service-api-contract", "kind": "dependency", "label": "auth-service-api-contract"} (a dependency on another team's API contract). External vendor example: {"id": "cn:project:dependency:stripe-api", "kind": "dependency", "label": "stripe-api"} (a third-party payment provider). Omit when the dependency is an internal milestone referenced via a milestone's depends_on field — those are tracked within the roadmap itself, not in the canonical registry.

trace.description: Traceability links connecting this roadmap to all upstream artifacts. Step 14 should include trace entries for each upstream artifact type consumed in Extraction Intent (e.g., FRs from Step 04, NFRs from Step 07, invariants from Step 06, threats from Step 11, capabilities from Step 01, governance/CI references from Steps 10/12). The specific trace types must be valid entries from the canon trace_type registry. Each entry must have type, id (matching the upstream ID), and note (naming the validating task).

items.description: A traceability reference for the roadmap.
